headline: High-risk filesystem and network asymmetry: Mentat can read/write shared code while ComfyUI is offline-only, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is not documented. ComfyUI is offline-only and has no clipboard/MCP surface, while Mentat reads files and uses stdin/stdout plus filesystem-based shared state. Any injection would require unusual manual file bridging or copy-paste, so the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies ComfyUI-generated text into Mentat prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace files, file-content prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories.
Do not paste ComfyUI outputs into Mentat prompts without review.
Use a read-only export step for any handoff file.
Add a short human review before Mentat consumes generated text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat can read filesystem contents and send them to a configured model provider, while ComfyUI touches models, embeddings, and workflow assets. In a shared workspace, Mentat can ingest ComfyUI artifacts and transmit them off-box; ComfyUI itself is offline-only, so the leakage path is one-way but real in default coding workflows.
conditions: IF ComfyUI artifacts are stored in a directory Mentat can read, those contents can be sent to the model provider.
IF the operator places secrets inside shared project files, Mentat may exfiltrate them through API calls.
mitigations: Store ComfyUI assets outside Mentat's working tree.
Remove secrets from any files Mentat can read.
Use a separate OS account for each agent.
Disable network access for Mentat during sensitive sessions if feasible.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat has filesystem write and git modification capability, and its shared state is via filesystem; ComfyUI also uses files for models and workflows. If both are pointed at the same directory, concurrent edits can overwrite assets or git state without locking. The pair therefore has a dangerous default conflict pathway, especially because Mentat supports multiple instances.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable directory, file clobbering is possible.
IF Mentat is used inside a git repo that ComfyUI also writes to, git-state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Keep ComfyUI model folders outside any git repo Mentat edits.
Run only one Mentat instance per workspace.
Use filesystem snapshots before concurrent work.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat is a coding assistant that proposes diffs and can act on file contents, so it may treat ComfyUI-generated workflows or text artifacts as authoritative inputs. ComfyUI can emit workflow files and model-selection artifacts, and Mentat can then propagate mistakes into code changes. This is a plausible default handoff, though not fully autonomous.
conditions: IF ComfyUI output is copied into Mentat as a source of truth, errors can cascade into edits.
IF Mentat is asked to implement changes from generated workflows without verification, incorrect assumptions can propagate.
mitigations: Require a human check before Mentat acts on ComfyUI output.
Keep generated artifacts labeled as untrusted.
Use a validation checklist for any handoff file.
Ask Mentat to summarize before editing.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. ComfyUI is offline-only and touches media/model assets, while Mentat sends code to a configured provider and handles API keys. The main compliance concern is local handling of source code and secrets, but the profiles do not show a direct regulated-data breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in files Mentat can read, provider transmission may create a compliance issue.
IF the operator uses Mentat on code containing secrets without redaction, retention policies may be implicated.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Mentat workspaces.
Redact secrets before editing sessions.
Confirm provider retention settings before use.
Keep ComfyUI assets and code repositories separate.
